focus: Clew: one send effect = compressor + tempo-synced delay + small reverb. One level follower drives the compression and (Blend) ducks the echoes and room while playing so tails swell in the gaps. Controls: Squeeze, Echo (synced note lengths), Space, Blend; page 2 Tone, Motion, Dry, Attack; Shift: Order (Comp first / FX first).

directions.brief: Subject built on P4 Stack in depth; drawing language: patent section.
Subject built on P10 Voice field; drawing language: hidden-line isometric.
Subject built on P15 Cell field; drawing language: star atlas.
Subject built on P1 Section drawing; drawing language: engineering schematic.
Subject built on P13 Capture; drawing language: oscilloscope trace. This pattern is outside the category's column: say why this machine is the exception, or say plainly it doesn't fit.

variants.subject: A stack of glass echo plates in section, receding into the screen: the front plate is the playing, held in a clamp, and each plate behind is one repeat, set back by the delay time, with the room as a hatched back wall the stack fades into.
controls: Squeeze: the clamp's jaws close on the front plate and press its height down, from loose to tight.
Echo: the plates' spacing is the note length (1/32 close, 1/2 far apart) and more plates stand as the repeats grow; at 0 only the front plate.
Space: the back wall recedes and gains hatching lines, from none to a deep, dense wall.
Blend: while playing, the plates behind the front one sink down out of the light; in the gaps they rise back.
Tone: the plates taper with depth: steeply (dark, top cut away) to the left, squarer to the right.
Motion: the plates sway left and right out of line with each other.
Dry: the front plate's height, down to a thin sliver at 0.
Attack: the clamp's lead-in bevel: long and gradual at slow attack, short and sharp at fast.
Order (Shift): the clamp moves from the front plate to around the whole stack.
variants.reference: library/theseus-tower (line drawing of a known object), P4 Stack in depth (MNMD DPRO-WAVE)
variants.risks: Plates in a stack can read as a wavetable display rather than echoes; a clamp is close to an icon if drawn loosely.

variants.subject: An isometric floor of slabs as the room: a note lands as a raised block at the front, its echoes are rows of lower blocks marching back across the floor at the delay spacing, and the reverb is a fine low relief that spreads from them.
controls: Squeeze: every block's height is clipped to a plateau that comes down as it rises, so tall and short notes even out.
Echo: the rows' spacing is the note length and their count the repeats; 0 leaves the floor flat behind the note.
Space: how far the relief spreads across the floor and how slowly it flattens.
Blend: while playing, the echo rows and relief sink into the floor; in the gaps they rise again.
Tone: the relief's fine detail: rough, many small bumps to the right, smooth broad swells to the left.
Motion: the echo rows bend sideways in a slow S across the floor.
Dry: the note's own front block, from full height to flush with the floor.
Attack: the plateau's edge: a soft ramp into the clip at slow attack, a hard step at fast.
Order (Shift): with FX first the plateau also caps the echo rows and relief, not only the note's block.
variants.risks: Close to toro's look, so the two machines may read as one; field-wide sinking on every note is costly in redraw.

variants.subject: A star chart of the send: the playing is a bright star plotted on the left, each echo a fainter star repeated along a dotted ecliptic at the delay spacing, and the room a scatter of square cell-stars around them, labelled like an atlas plate.
controls: Squeeze: the main star's magnitude marks pull in, so loud and soft notes plot the same size.
Echo: the copies' spacing along the ecliptic is the note length and their count the repeats.
Space: how many cell-stars fill the field and how far they spread.
Blend: while playing the copies and cells dim to faint; in the gaps they brighten back.
Tone: the cell-stars' grain: single fine points to the right, clumped runs to the left.
Motion: the ecliptic wavers, its dotted line bending.
Dry: the main star's size, down to a hollow ring at 0.
Attack: the main star's halo: tight at fast attack, a soft wide ring at slow.
Order (Shift): the atlas plate's label switches between COMP FIRST and FX FIRST, and the magnitude marks move to the whole field.
variants.reference: library/meikyu-orrery (an atlas-like plate), toro's first Taurus chart in labyrinth
variants.risks: Brightness-only changes (Blend, Space) lean on shade; an atlas with no sky subject is decoration.

variants.subject: A cutaway schematic of one box: a gain valve the playing passes through, a tape loop with a moving playback head for the echoes, and a coil spring tank for the room, linked by a single lever from the level follower that dips the tape and spring outputs while playing.
controls: Squeeze: the valve's gate closes across the signal path, from fully open to a narrow slot.
Echo: the playback head slides along the tape away from the record head; the distance is the note length, and more loops of tape show as repeats grow; at 0 the head lifts off.
Space: the spring stretches and gains coils, from a short stub to a long tank.
Blend: the follower's lever tips further while playing, pressing the tape and spring outputs down; it lifts in the gaps.
Tone: a damper pad moves onto the spring and tape, from touching hard (dark) to clear and then a thin felt (bright).
Motion: the tape's guide roller swings, wavering the tape path.
Dry: a bypass link from input to output thickens from absent to full width.
Attack: the lever's spring: a stiff short spring at fast attack, a long soft one at slow.
Order (Shift): the valve slides from before the tape and spring to after them on the path.
variants.reference: library/theseus-tower (geometric line drawing of real apparatus), P1 Section drawing (MNMD MD KIT)
variants.risks: Many parts to fit in 480 x 220 at legible weights; three mechanisms may compete for the brightest element.

variants.subject: The rule drawn as a scope: the playing's level is a bright envelope trace across the screen and the tails are a second, finer trace held beneath it, captured under the playing while it's loud and rising into the space it leaves in the gaps.
controls: Squeeze: a threshold line drops and the bright trace's peaks flatten against it.
Echo: decaying copies of each peak repeat to the right at the note length's spacing.
Space: the fine trace's tail stretches longer and smoother after each peak.
Blend: how far the bright trace pushes the fine one down where they overlap.
Tone: the fine trace's grain: jagged high detail to the right, smooth to the left.
Motion: the echo copies drift a little early and late around their spacing.
Dry: the bright trace's height, down to a flat line at 0.
Attack: the slope of the flattening at each peak's start: a sharp corner at fast attack, a rounded lead-in at slow.
Order (Shift): the threshold line extends under the fine trace too.
variants.reference: P3 Trace as subject, library/meikyu-capture (P13: draw the machine's own rule)
variants.risks: Outside the effect column for P13: its case is that Clew's rule (the playing holds the tails down) is itself a capture; but a scope trace is P3's ground, and two traces may read as a meter.
